As our Chief Philanthropy Officer, you will serve on the executive Senior Leadership Group (SLG) and oversee the affiliated fundraising foundations in various States, including direct supervision of the newly formed system-wide Health Foundation.

Minimum of five (5) years of management experience.

jobs.description:
Senior Director of Executive Communications, EVP/COO Office

Loyola Marymount University (LMU) is seeking a strategic, experienced communications leader to serve as the Senior Director of Executive Communications for the EVP/COO
. This position serves as the principal communications strategist and senior communications lead for the EVP/COO, working closely with senior leadership and LMU’s Marketing, Communications, and External Relations (MarComm) division.

The Senior Director will serve as a trusted strategic thought partner to the EVP/COO, helping shape, prioritize, and communicate the executive agenda supporting university administration, operations, organizational effectiveness, institutional reputation, and external engagement. The role advises on narrative, message strategy, timing, audience segmentation, channel selection, operational change communications, and sensitive issues.

Key Responsibilities

Executive Communications Strategy
Serve as the principal communications strategist and trusted advisor to the EVP/COO.
Develop communications strategies and roadmaps supporting key operational and organizational priorities.
Develop an executive visibility strategy, including speaking engagements, thought leadership, digital platforms, and other high-impact channels.
Translate executive priorities into clear communications objectives, integrated plans, editorial calendars, and measurable deliverables.
Anticipate communications needs related to complex, cross-functional, and high-visibility matters.
Exercise independent editorial and strategic judgment while appropriately escalating sensitive issues.

Executive Writing & Content Development
Develop and maintain an authentic executive voice for the EVP/COO aligned with LMU’s mission, brand, and tone.
Research, write, edit, and finalize executive communications, including campus messages, leadership updates, speeches, remarks, correspondence, presentations, reports, FAQs, blog posts, and op-eds.
Develop executive digital and social media content and engagement strategies.
Translate complex operational, financial, policy, technical, risk, and organizational information into clear, compelling, audience-appropriate communications.
Maintain high standards for accuracy, tone, fact-checking, quality assurance, and editorial consistency.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
Serve as the communications liaison between the Office of the EVP/COO and LMU’s MarComm division.
Partner with senior communications leaders supporting the President, Provost, and other university leaders to ensure cohesive institutional messaging.
Collaborate with leaders and subject matter experts across operations, finance, HR, IT, facilities, campus safety, auxiliary services, external relations, and other areas.

Change & Issues Communications
Lead or support communications related to operational change, organizational transitions, complex institutional decisions, and other high-impact or time-sensitive developments.
Prepare message maps, stakeholder briefs, FAQs, scenario plans, and rapid-response materials for sensitive or reputationally significant matters.
Support issues management and, when needed, crisis or emergency communications planning and execution.

Communications Innovation & AI
Integrate AI-enabled and emerging communications tools into research, synthesis, drafting, content development, analytics, and workflow management.
Build efficient, human-centered communications workflows that improve productivity, quality, and turnaround time.
Apply sound judgment regarding privacy, confidentiality, accuracy, accessibility, ethics, and institutional policies when using AI.
Use audience feedback and performance analytics to assess effectiveness and inform communications strategy.
Stay current on emerging executive communications practices, platforms, and AI-enabled productivity tools.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, English, marketing, or a related field; master’s degree preferred.
10+ years of progressively responsible communications experience
, including substantial experience supporting C-suite, cabinet-level, presidential, provost-level, or other senior executive leadership in a complex organization.
Exceptional executive writing, editing, storytelling, and strategic communications skills.
Demonstrated ability to translate complex operational, financial, policy, technical, or organizational information into clear and compelling communications.
Experience developing integrated communications strategies and managing multiple high-visibility projects in a fast-paced environment.
Strong executive presence, judgment, discretion, maturity, and professionalism when handling sensitive or confidential matters.
Proven ability to influence across functions, build strong partnerships with senior leaders, and operate effectively without direct authority.
Familiarity with communications analytics and measurement.
Experience using AI tools and emerging communications technologies to improve efficiency, synthesis, drafting, content quality, or decision support.
Experience in higher education or another mission-driven, reputation-sensitive, and operationally complex institution is preferred
.
Ability to adapt to changing priorities, including occasional evening or weekend support as needed.

Why LMU?

This is an opportunity to join a collaborative communications team and play a critical role in helping a senior university executive communicate complex priorities with clarity, credibility, and purpose. Communications at LMU are viewed as a leadership discipline that builds clarity, trust, transparency, alignment, and institutional momentum.

Role Overview

The Director of Strategic Partnerships & Development leads ISTH's efforts to build and diversify non-dues revenue in service of the Society's mission to advance the understanding, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of thrombotic and bleeding disorders worldwide. Reporting to the Executive Director & CEO, the Director will design and build ISTH's strategic partnerships and development function from the ground up, spanning corporate and industry partnerships, sponsorship, education and research support, and institutional giving. The Director will cultivate durable, mission-aligned relationships across a global partner community while establishing a sustainable foundation for long-term growth.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Revenue Diversification

Develop and lead ISTH's strategic partnerships and revenue-diversification strategy, reducing concentration risk across partners, sectors, and revenue types.
Analyze the current revenue mix, benchmark against peer international societies, and set measurable growth and diversification targets.
Build a balanced portfolio of revenue streams impacting areas across annual congress, education, research, policy and awareness, institutional giving.

Corporate & Industry Partnerships

Design and launch a tiered Strategic Partner Program that converts episodic sponsorships into multi-year, year-round relationships.
Cultivate, negotiate, and steward partnerships across pharmaceutical, diagnostics, medical device, and digital-health sectors.
Serve as the senior relationship owner for ISTH's largest corporate partners, engaging in medical-affairs, commercial, and foundation counterparts.

Institutional Giving & Development

Establish a funding pillar including research and fellowship funds, foundation grants, and institutional giving that diversifies beyond corporate support.
Partner with foundations, and intergovernmental/NGO funders (e.g., WHO) on global health and LMIC-access programs.

Grant Writing & Proposal Development

Lead the development of high-quality grant proposals, letters of inquiry, and funding applications to foundations, corporate foundations, and other funders in support of ISTH's research, education, awareness, and global-health priorities.
Translate ISTH initiatives — fellowships, research funds, LMIC-access programs, and priority strategic initiatives — into fundable proposals tailored to each funder's mission, guidelines, and reporting expectations.
Manage the full grants lifecycle: funder prospecting and cultivation, proposal and budget development submission, and post-award stewardship and reporting, in partnership with internal departments.
Partner with program and scientific staff to source proposal content while preserving the scientific-independence firewall for funder-supported programs.

Congress Events & Sponsorships

Develop and maximize Congress-related partnership and sponsorship opportunities, including exhibition, industry-supported symposia, digital and hybrid placements, in close collaboration with the Meetings & Events team.
Develop year-round partnership opportunities around World Thrombosis Day, the Women's Health Initiative, and other mission-aligned platforms in collaboration with public affairs, marketing, education, and other relevant teams.

Compliance, Ethics & Scientific Independence

Uphold and operationalize the scientific-independence firewall so that no funder influences SSC standards, guidelines/guidance, editorial decisions, or the scientific program.
Ensure all relationships comply with the strictest applicable global transparency and disclosure regimes.
Develop and apply grant-acceptance and partner-vetting policies, escalating edge cases through the appropriate governance channels.

Team Leadership & Operations

Build and lead the Strategic Partnerships team through a phased approach aligned with revenue growth and organizational priorities; set goals, coach, and develop staff.
Stand up the function's infrastructure — database, partnership prospectus and rate card, contract and approval workflows, and reporting dashboards.
Own pipeline discipline, forecasting, and impact reporting with support from finance team; ensure relationships are held institutionally.

Knowledge & Skill Requirements

The Director of Strategic Partnerships & Business Development will be a seasoned leader with demonstrated success in strategic leadership, organizational management, and partnership development. This person will combine:

Advanced degrees or a scientific/clinical background required.
5+ years of progressive experience in partnerships, innovative programming, grants, including relationship ownership.
Demonstrated success building and diversifying non-dues or grants revenue and converting transactional sponsorships into multi-year partnerships.
International/global experience and cultural fluency.
Fluency in healthcare funder and industry relations and the compliance environment governing industry–society relationships.
Experience building teams, systems, and pipelines from an early state.
Exceptional relationship-building, negotiation, and written/verbal communication skills.

Core Competencies

Strategic acumen — sees the whole revenue portfolio and builds durable value, not one-off wins.
Ethical judgment & mission alignment — protects Society’s independence and reputation as the first consideration in every deal.
Relationship cultivation & stewardship — builds trust with senior partners and turns relationships into long-term, institutional commitments.
Global mindset & cultural competence — works fluently across regions, cultures, and markets in a truly international organization.
Financial literacy & data-driven decision-making — sets targets, reads the numbers, and manages a pipeline with rigor and transparency.
Team leadership & collaboration — builds and develops a team and collaborates across a matrixed, volunteer-led organization.

ISTH CORE VALUES

The ideal candidate will actively embody ISTH's core values in all aspects of leadership and decision-making.

Trust – Demonstrated integrity, transparency, and consistency in all dealings
Collaboration – Valuing diverse perspectives and partnering effectively with volunteer leadership and stakeholders
Respect – Inclusive leadership and thoughtful engagement across disciplines, regions, and backgrounds

At the conclusion of the term, there may be an opportunity to transition the position to a permanent role, continue the position as structured, or adjust its scope, responsibilities, or structure to align with and best support the evolving needs and strategic priories of the organization.

Who We Are:

Youth Empowerment Project engages underserved young people through community-based education, mentoring, employment readiness, and enrichment programs to help them develop skills and strengthen ties to family and community. YEP has served young people and families across the Greater New Orleans area for more than two decades. Through four integrated program areas, YEP provides comprehensive, community-based services grounded in the belief that support should be individualized and opportunities should be accessible to all. Each year, we serve more than 1,000 participants across 13 parishes through programs operating at different five locations. Our core purpose is to empower young people to improve their lives and the lives of others.

Our Culture and Values:

We are a community of professionals who believe in the power of collaboration, curiosity, and self-care. Our work is anchored in Respect, Kindness, and Integrity
with Accountability and Progress
shaping how we work. We learn continuously, invest in meaningful relationships, and care for ourselves so we can better serve one another and the young people who count on us. 

The Opportunity:

The Youth Empowerment Project (YEP) is seeking an experienced, strategic, relationship-driven leader to serve as our next Chief Development Officer.

This is an exciting opportunity to join one of Greater New Orleans' leading youth-serving organizations as we enter our next chapter of growth. Guided by a five-year strategic plan, a strong financial foundation, and an engaged Board of Directors, YEP is well positioned to build on its 21-year legacy and expand its impact for young people and families across the region.

Following a successful leadership transition from YEP’s longstanding CEO/Co-Founder, the organization has implemented a thoughtful co-leadership model with a CEO and President, designed to preserve the organization's values, culture, and institutional knowledge while positioning it for the future. The Chief Development Officer will partner closely with both the CEO and President, joining a collaborative executive team that combines deep institutional knowledge with a shared commitment to innovation, organizational sustainability, and lasting impact for young people.

As a member of YEP's Senior Leadership Team, the Chief Development Officer will lead the organization's comprehensive fundraising, communications, and external engagement strategy while partnering closely with the CEO, President, and Board of Directors to grow philanthropic support and advance YEP's mission.
The CDO will oversee and continue building a talented development team, lead fundraising strategies across individual, corporate, foundation, government, and special event revenue, and personally cultivate and develop key donor and stakeholder relationships. This leader will also help strengthen the systems, infrastructure, and culture of philanthropy that will support YEP's continued growth for years to come.
YEP enters this next chapter from a position of organizational strength. Supported by an engaged, 23 member Board of Directors, a collaborative and seasoned leadership team, and a passionate and dedicated staff, the next Chief Development Officer has the opportunity to build upon a solid foundation while helping shape the future of one of the region’s leading youth-serving organizations.

This role is ideal for an experienced fundraiser who enjoys both strategic leadership and frontline fundraising. We recognize that exceptional candidates come from a variety of professional backgrounds, including Chief Development Officer, Development Director, Executive Director, CEO, and other senior leadership roles with fundraising responsibility. We welcome candidates with diverse professional backgrounds whose experience is aligned the required qualifications for this position.
We are seeking someone who thrives on building and maintaining strong relationships, collaborating with others, developing high-performing teams, and inspiring individuals and organizations to invest in a brighter future for young people in our community.

: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1PqqsM00IzKZjUshxR6lbUZXWXUkaJ74f/view?usp=sharing

This position is responsible for annual fundraising from individuals and organizations at the $24,999 level and below, through annual giving appeals and individual portfolio outreach. The Associate Director works closely with the AVP for University Advancement to develop fundraising priorities and execute annual fundraising plans for MBKU and the three programs. This position actively manages a prospect portfolio of 75-125 individuals, identifies and qualifies new prospects, and oversees the annual solicitations and stewardship for scholarship donors. Additionally, the Associate Director works closely with the Alumni Council and affiliated program-based alumni societies and the AVP, to develop programs to engage alumni and build relationships to secure private support and build alumni pride.

Essential Duties And Responsi­­bilities

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Articulate the case for support with effectiveness; communicate the priorities, goals and mission of the university.
Articulate the value of gifts to MBKU and the three programs to meet programmatic fundraising priorities and goals.
Manage and actively engage a portfolio of approximately 75-125 alumni and organizational prospects. Conduct strategic outreach to identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit and steward donors.
Develop and execute individualized cultivation, solicitation and stewardship strategies designed to advance prospects through the major gift pipeline. Performance expectations include consistently achieving monthly, quarterly, and annual metrics including but not limited to outreach attempts, number of meaningful donor visits, substantive donor conversations, gift solicitations, and other key metrics as defined by UA leadership.
Develop proposals and other necessary written collateral to secure private support for annual campus and program priorities including scholarships, sponsorships, programmatic needs and other college based and MBKU programmatic fundraising priorities.
Write, develop, and manage the execution of annual giving appeals.
Responsible for developing increasing levels of involvement and support among donors and prospects utilizing best practices for cultivation and stewardship through regular correspondence and contacts in person, by phone, mail and email.
Assist with annual giving, scholarship, Alumni Council and Club engagement activities and events. Assist the AVP in developing programs to increase engagement activities for alumni, including alumni awards programming, regional receptions, alumni giving clubs and other volunteer opportunities that align with institutional and program-based priorities.
Contribute to the overall strategic plan for the office of University Advancement as it relates to Alumni Relations, scholarship fundraising, stewardship of donors, and annual fund outreach.

Participate in professional conference alumni receptions and programs.

Demonstrated organizational skills to achieve timely progress on multiple simultaneous complex projects, meet deadlines and maintain a high level of productivity.

About The University

SEE YOURSELF HERE

Located on a beautiful, seven-acre campus in Fullerton, California, MBKU is an independent, private, non-profit, accredited educational institution. MBKU is home to the Southern California College of Optometry, the School of PA Studies, College of Pharmacy and the Doctor of Medical Science Program (DMSc) . He made very significant and long-standing contributions in his field of care, in California and throughout the nation.

In the early ‘70s the College moved to its current home in Fullerton, CA and was renamed Southern California College of Optometry. At Marshall B. Ketchum University, we have led the way in interprofessional healthcare, building on a century of experience as an optometry school. In 2012, the first Physician Assistant program in Orange County was added, followed by the College of Pharmacy program in 2014. jobs.description:
Organization Overview:
Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity
Phi Kappa Tau is entering an exciting period of growth and opportunity, as it builds on a 120-year tradition of championing brotherhood, learning, ethical leadership, and exemplary character. The fraternity serves 4,300 undergraduate members at approximately 80 chapters, and has about 100,000 alumni members. While the Phi Kappa Tau fraternity experience begins on campus, it lasts a lifetime: throughout their lives, members form meaningful friendships, find opportunities to lead and serve, and build powerful personal and professional networks.

Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity (the Fraternity) is a 501(c)(7) nonprofit headquartered in Oxford, Ohio with a national staff of approximately 15 professionals and an elected Board, known as the National Council. It supports campus chapters and members with leadership development, educational programming, recruitment, chapter operations, national events, and alumni programs. The Fraternity is funded from undergraduate member fees, event registration fees, and an educational grant from the Phi Kappa Tau Foundation (the Foundation). The Foundation is an affiliated 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit organization with its own Board of Trustees and professional staff. The Fraternity collaborates with the Foundation on communications, events, alumni programming, and other areas where the two organizations have shared interests.
In its next phase of growth, the Fraternity’s strategic plan, Building the Phi Kappa Tau Experience , centers on strengthening existing chapters, expanding to new campuses, deepening undergraduate and alumni engagement, broadening leadership and learning opportunities, and creating greater value for members throughout their lives.

This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help shape the Phi Kappa Tau member experience at a time when meaningful personal connection and ethical leadership are more valuable than ever before. The next CEO will bring Phi Kappa Tau’s recognized leadership education to a new generation of students while strengthening the bonds of brotherhood among all members.

Position Summary:
Chief Executive Officer

Phi Kappa Tau seeks an energetic, growth-minded Chief Executive Officer to champion its mission, support its members, and lead the organization into its next era of impact. Reporting to the National Council, the CEO will lead the execution of the organization’s strategic plan and serve as a highly relational leader who is equally comfortable working both in and on the organization. They will build credibility across a diverse community, from undergraduate members and young staff to alumni volunteers and university administrators.

Internally, the CEO will lead a national staff and oversee a complex organization with an annual budget of approximately $3 million. This leader will bring financial discipline and operational rigor, with particular attention to budgeting, forecasting, accounts receivable, and financial reporting. They will provide the mentorship, coaching, structure, and accountability needed to help both early career and experienced staff members grow and perform at a high level.
Externally, the CEO will focus on growth and engagement across the Fraternity. They will help existing chapters grow and thrive while executing our strategy to expand to new campuses. As a strong trust-builder and communicator, they will strengthen relationships with university administrators, engage Phi Kappa Tau’s alumni, expand its volunteer network, and create more opportunities for lifelong connection to the Fraternity.

The ideal candidate will bring an appreciation for fraternity and lifelong brotherhood and exposure to collegiate fraternal organizations – whether through membership, professional leadership, volunteer service, or board involvement. Experience within business, membership organizations, or nonprofits is likewise valued. This is an opportunity to pair seasoned leadership with fresh thinking to shape the future of Phi Kappa Tau for generations to come.

Key responsibilities

Strategic Leadership, Governance & Growth

Partner with the National Council on strategy, policy, and governance, providing timely reporting on organizational performance, finances, strategic plan progress, and emerging risks.
Lead implementation of Phi Kappa Tau’s strategic plan, establishing measurable goals and translating priorities into clear organizational and staff work plans.
Develop and execute strategies to grow undergraduate membership, strengthen retention, and expand Phi Kappa Tau to new campuses.
Identify, execute, and evaluate new programs and approaches that advance strategic priorities, using data to understand results and scale what works.

Organizational, Financial & People Leadership

Lead the Fraternity’s approximately 15-person staff, including org chart design, hiring, performance management, compensation, professional development, and mentorship of both early-career and experienced professionals.
Provide overall financial stewardship, including annual budgeting, cash flow management, fee-setting for programs and membership, collections, balance sheet management, and ongoing financial performance monitoring.
Strengthen organizational systems and processes, using data and emerging technology (including AI) to improve efficiency, reporting, decision-making, and the member experience.
Oversee proactive risk prevention, disciplinary issues, legal matters, and crisis response, stepping in directly to support chapters and volunteers when significant issues arise.

Chapters, Members & Volunteers

Ensure chapters receive responsive, high-quality support and resources that help them recruit and retain members, develop leaders, and operate effectively.
Build and sustain Phi Kappa Tau’s volunteer network by recruiting and engaging volunteers, matching individuals with meaningful opportunities, and supporting volunteer boards and committees.
Oversee national events and educational programming, including National Convention and leadership and learning programs.
Improve the member experience by modernizing existing programs, services, communications, and digital resources, and finding innovative new ways to create value for undergraduate and alumni members.

External Relations, Communications & Partnerships

Serve as a visible public face and ambassador for Phi Kappa Tau at chapter, alumni, national, and interfraternal events and within the broader fraternity and sorority community.
Strengthen relationships with host colleges and universities, including direct engagement with administrators when chapters need support or challenges arise.
Partner with the Foundation Executive Director on joint initiatives and collaborative planning.
Lead consistent, transparent, multi-channel communication with undergraduate members, alumni, volunteers, parents, university partners, and other stakeholders.

Leadership & Competency Expectations

Dynamic Communicator & Trusted Bridge-Builder

An engaging leader who can connect authentically across the Phi Kappa Tau community. They will adapt their style to different audiences, listen with empathy, and skillfully navigate difficult conversations, whether navigating sensitive issues, supporting a chapter leader through a challenge, or advocating for the fraternity’s interests. A compelling storyteller and ambassador, they can also command a room, inspire new members, and represent Phi Kappa Tau with confidence before a range of audiences.

Coach, Mentor & Team Builder

Leads with a coaching mindset, creating an environment where a small, relatively young staff can learn, take ownership, and pursue ambitious goals. This leader will recognize that some team members are early in their careers and will provide the mentorship, feedback, professional development, and clear expectations the staff needs to succeed. They will build accountability while fostering a culture of trust, collaboration, and shared purpose.

Innovative & Growth-Minded Leader

Brings fresh thinking to how Phi Kappa Tau grows and creates meaningful value for its members. This leader will challenge longstanding approaches and critically evaluate processes, resources, and programs with an eye toward what today’s students and alumni need. Job Description: Founding Chief Executive Officer 

Confidential | Full-Time | Remote with Travel
A well-capitalized, early-stage venture is seeking a Founding Chief Executive Officer to build and launch a mission-driven specialty services platform addressing a significant unmet need among college students and young adults. The founder has established the vision and committed the capital. The CEO's mandate is to transform that vision into a scalable organization. We are seeking a hands-on builder-operator who has personally launched, built, scaled, turned around, or fundamentally transformed an operating business. The Founding CEO will lead the company from concept through the successful launch of its first flagship location by building the founding team, establishing the operating model, developing critical external partnerships, and creating the foundation for future growth.
Duties & Responsibilities: 

Lead the company from pre-launch through the successful opening and operation of its first location.
Translate the founder’s vision into clear priorities, milestones, metrics, and execution.
Recruit, build, and lead the founding team.
Partner closely with leadership to build an operating model that delivers a differentiated, high-quality service experience while maintaining the highest standards of quality and integrity.
Build the company’s early operating systems, management cadence, and culture of accountability.
Personally establish strategic partnerships with colleges, universities, institutional leaders, referral partners, and other organizations critical to the company's long-term success.
Develop a deep understanding of the customer journey—including what creates urgency, builds trust, drives engagement, and creates long-term value.
Immerse deeply in the company’s marketing and demand-generation efforts, ensuring a diversified pipeline of qualified leads sufficient to support strong utilization across locations. 
Build, staff, and oversee a high-performing centralized call center responsible for converting inquiries into customers and supporting future locations as the company scales.
Own the commercial success of the flagship location, including customer demand, operating economics, and the path toward a repeatable multi-location model.
Learn rapidly from the first launch and translate those lessons into a foundation for future expansion.

Qualifications:
We are more interested in what you have built than where you have worked.
Founding-stage commitment. This is not a traditional 9-to-5 role. You are prepared for the intensity of building a company from the ground up, including nights, weekends, and significant travel when critical launches, hiring, partnerships, or operating milestones require it. 
Repeated builder evidence. You can point to businesses, locations, markets, teams, or operating models you personally helped create, launch, scale, turn around, or fundamentally transform.
High agency. You see gaps and act. You are comfortable moving before all answers are known and do not need a large team or established infrastructure to make progress.
Operational rigor. You turn vision into priorities, milestones, metrics, accountability, and execution.
Team-building ability. You have personally recruited and led strong people and can attract talent before there is a well-known brand behind you.
Partnership-building strength. You are willing to step away from behind a desk and travel as needed to open doors, build trust, and develop relationships that move the organization forward. 
Commercial judgment. You understand meaningful parts of the commercial engine, including customer demand, pricing, revenue, P&L, growth, and/or unit economics.
Low-ego conviction. You can challenge a strong founder, be challenged in return, make decisions, and move forward without politics or a need for personal authorship.

Your Background: 

There is no single required industry path for this role. We are significantly more interested in evidence of building than industry pedigree .
Relevant experience may come from multi-site services, consumer healthcare, specialty care, education or young-adult services, hospitality, franchising, founder-led companies, PE-backed growth businesses, or other environments where you have personally built and operated something. You are a relentless generalist–curious, resourceful, commercially minded, and comfortable driving across functions. You find a way forward when the answer is unclear and treat “no” as another problem to solve.
The Motivation:

This work must matter to you. We are building an organization designed to intervene earlier in the lives of college students and young adults facing an increasingly consequential challenge. We believe earlier action can fundamentally change life trajectories, and we are looking for a leader who is energized by building an organization capable of doing exactly that. 
Compensation:
The anticipated base salary range for this role is $150,000–$275,000
, plus performance-based incentive compensation and meaningful equity participation. We are intentionally flexible on base to find the right builder. This role is designed for a leader who values substantial performance-based upside and meaningful equity participation and is motivated by the opportunity to share in the enterprise value they help create. The final compensation package will reflect the successful candidate’s experience and the scope of responsibility they bring to the role. 
Location & Travel:
This is a remote, work-from-home role with meaningful travel. The CEO must be willing to travel regularly to support the launch of the first location, develop critical external partnerships, meet with the founding team, and represent the company externally. This is a highly hands-on, relationship-driven role that cannot be built entirely from behind a screen. 
Why Join?

This is an opportunity to join at the beginning. The Founding CEO will have the opportunity to shape the company, build the founding team and culture, launch the first location, establish the operating model, and participate meaningfully in the value they help create.

Organization Overview:
Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity
Phi Kappa Tau is entering an exciting period of growth and opportunity, as it builds on a 120-year tradition of championing brotherhood, learning, ethical leadership, and exemplary character. The fraternity serves 4,300 undergraduate members at approximately 80 chapters, and has about 100,000 alumni members. While the Phi Kappa Tau fraternity experience begins on campus, it lasts a lifetime: throughout their lives, members form meaningful friendships, find opportunities to lead and serve, and build powerful personal and professional networks.

Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity (the Fraternity) is a 501(c)(7) nonprofit headquartered in Oxford, Ohio with a national staff of approximately 15 professionals and an elected Board, known as the National Council. It supports campus chapters and members with leadership development, educational programming, recruitment, chapter operations, national events, and alumni programs. The Fraternity is funded from undergraduate member fees, event registration fees, and an educational grant from the Phi Kappa Tau Foundation (the Foundation). The Foundation is an affiliated 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit organization with its own Board of Trustees and professional staff. The Fraternity collaborates with the Foundation on communications, events, alumni programming, and other areas where the two organizations have shared interests.
In its next phase of growth, the Fraternity’s strategic plan, Building the Phi Kappa Tau Experience , centers on strengthening existing chapters, expanding to new campuses, deepening undergraduate and alumni engagement, broadening leadership and learning opportunities, and creating greater value for members throughout their lives.

This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help shape the Phi Kappa Tau member experience at a time when meaningful personal connection and ethical leadership are more valuable than ever before. The next CEO will bring Phi Kappa Tau’s recognized leadership education to a new generation of students while strengthening the bonds of brotherhood among all members.

Position Summary:
Chief Executive Officer

Phi Kappa Tau seeks an energetic, growth-minded Chief Executive Officer to champion its mission, support its members, and lead the organization into its next era of impact. Reporting to the National Council, the CEO will lead the execution of the organization’s strategic plan and serve as a highly relational leader who is equally comfortable working both in and on the organization. They will build credibility across a diverse community, from undergraduate members and young staff to alumni volunteers and university administrators.

Internally, the CEO will lead a national staff and oversee a complex organization with an annual budget of approximately $3 million. This leader will bring financial discipline and operational rigor, with particular attention to budgeting, forecasting, accounts receivable, and financial reporting. They will provide the mentorship, coaching, structure, and accountability needed to help both early career and experienced staff members grow and perform at a high level.
Externally, the CEO will focus on growth and engagement across the Fraternity. They will help existing chapters grow and thrive while executing our strategy to expand to new campuses. As a strong trust-builder and communicator, they will strengthen relationships with university administrators, engage Phi Kappa Tau’s alumni, expand its volunteer network, and create more opportunities for lifelong connection to the Fraternity.

The ideal candidate will bring an appreciation for fraternity and lifelong brotherhood and exposure to collegiate fraternal organizations – whether through membership, professional leadership, volunteer service, or board involvement. Experience within business, membership organizations, or nonprofits is likewise valued. This is an opportunity to pair seasoned leadership with fresh thinking to shape the future of Phi Kappa Tau for generations to come.

Key responsibilities

Strategic Leadership, Governance & Growth

Partner with the National Council on strategy, policy, and governance, providing timely reporting on organizational performance, finances, strategic plan progress, and emerging risks.
Lead implementation of Phi Kappa Tau’s strategic plan, establishing measurable goals and translating priorities into clear organizational and staff work plans.
Develop and execute strategies to grow undergraduate membership, strengthen retention, and expand Phi Kappa Tau to new campuses.
Identify, execute, and evaluate new programs and approaches that advance strategic priorities, using data to understand results and scale what works.

Organizational, Financial & People Leadership

Lead the Fraternity’s approximately 15-person staff, including org chart design, hiring, performance management, compensation, professional development, and mentorship of both early-career and experienced professionals.
Provide overall financial stewardship, including annual budgeting, cash flow management, fee-setting for programs and membership, collections, balance sheet management, and ongoing financial performance monitoring.
Strengthen organizational systems and processes, using data and emerging technology (including AI) to improve efficiency, reporting, decision-making, and the member experience.
Oversee proactive risk prevention, disciplinary issues, legal matters, and crisis response, stepping in directly to support chapters and volunteers when significant issues arise.

Chapters, Members & Volunteers

Ensure chapters receive responsive, high-quality support and resources that help them recruit and retain members, develop leaders, and operate effectively.
Build and sustain Phi Kappa Tau’s volunteer network by recruiting and engaging volunteers, matching individuals with meaningful opportunities, and supporting volunteer boards and committees.
Oversee national events and educational programming, including National Convention and leadership and learning programs.
Improve the member experience by modernizing existing programs, services, communications, and digital resources, and finding innovative new ways to create value for undergraduate and alumni members.

External Relations, Communications & Partnerships

Serve as a visible public face and ambassador for Phi Kappa Tau at chapter, alumni, national, and interfraternal events and within the broader fraternity and sorority community.
Strengthen relationships with host colleges and universities, including direct engagement with administrators when chapters need support or challenges arise.
Partner with the Foundation Executive Director on joint initiatives and collaborative planning.
Lead consistent, transparent, multi-channel communication with undergraduate members, alumni, volunteers, parents, university partners, and other stakeholders.

Leadership & Competency Expectations

Dynamic Communicator & Trusted Bridge-Builder

An engaging leader who can connect authentically across the Phi Kappa Tau community. They will adapt their style to different audiences, listen with empathy, and skillfully navigate difficult conversations, whether navigating sensitive issues, supporting a chapter leader through a challenge, or advocating for the fraternity’s interests. A compelling storyteller and ambassador, they can also command a room, inspire new members, and represent Phi Kappa Tau with confidence before a range of audiences.

Coach, Mentor & Team Builder

Leads with a coaching mindset, creating an environment where a small, relatively young staff can learn, take ownership, and pursue ambitious goals. This leader will recognize that some team members are early in their careers and will provide the mentorship, feedback, professional development, and clear expectations the staff needs to succeed. They will build accountability while fostering a culture of trust, collaboration, and shared purpose.

Innovative & Growth-Minded Leader

Brings fresh thinking to how Phi Kappa Tau grows and creates meaningful value for its members. This leader will challenge longstanding approaches and critically evaluate processes, resources, and programs with an eye toward what today’s students and alumni need. They will strengthen existing chapters, expand to new campuses, and explore ways to diversify revenue sources.

Decisive, Adaptable & Collaborative Leader

Comfortable leading within a complex environment where decision-making involves varied stakeholders: student members, alumni, elected leadership, volunteers, and university administrators. This leader will listen to different perspectives and build buy-in while also knowing when it is time to make a decision and move forward. They are comfortable recognizing gaps in expertise and leveraging volunteers and outside experts. They will be responsive and consistent in their follow-through, working effectively with the National Council and volunteer leaders while navigating change and competing priorities.

Location, Compensation and Benefits

Phi Kappa Tau’s headquarters is located in Oxford, Ohio, and the organization welcomes candidates based in or around the Greater Cincinnati area. There is a strong preference for a CEO who can maintain a regular and visible presence in the Executive Offices, working alongside the staff and providing in-person mentorship, particularly to early-career team members. The role includes regular travel of approximately 10 - 25% to engage with chapters, members, alumni, volunteers, university partners, and attend national events, as well as occasional evening and weekend commitments.
Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. Phi Kappa Tau offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental and vision coverage, paid time off, employer-paid life and disability insurance, and a 401(k) plan with an employer match.

Team-building ability. You have personally recruited and led strong people and can attract talent before there is a well-known brand behind you.

Low-ego conviction. You can challenge a strong founder, be challenged in return, make decisions, and move forward without politics or a need for personal authorship.

The East Central Iowa Workforce Development Board (ECIWDB) is seeking a dynamic and self-motivated Part-Time Executive Director
to lead and support the implementation of our workforce development mission across the region. This position offers a highly flexible work schedule, averaging approximately 25 hours per week
, with significant autonomy and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on workforce development throughout East Central Iowa.

About the Role:

The Executive Director is responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Board, strategic planning efforts, compliance oversight, and stakeholder engagement. This role serves as the primary liaison between the Board, workforce partners, state agencies, employers, educational institutions, and community stakeholders to ensure workforce development activities align with the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA), state requirements, and Board priorities. This position requires occasional on-site work at the American Job Centers located in Cedar Rapids and Iowa City
and periodic travel throughout the East Central Iowa workforce region. Applicants must reside within the ECIWDB service area, which includes Benton, Cedar, Iowa, Johnson, Jones, Linn, and Washington counties.

Core Responsibilities:

Provide leadership and coordination for Board operations and initiatives.
Supervise and support part-time Board staff member.
Coordinate and prepare materials for quarterly Board meetings, Executive Committee meetings, and four monthly working committee meetings.
Lead implementation and updates of the Board's local strategic plan.
Monitor workforce trends, labor market information, and regional workforce needs to inform Board decision-making.
Facilitate collaboration among employers, education partners, workforce agencies, economic development organizations, and other stakeholders.
Oversee local monitoring activities and assist with state monitoring and compliance reviews.
Ensure compliance with WIOA regulations, Board policies, and applicable federal and state requirements.
Support board development by providing workforce and economic insights that help inform strategic direction and policy decisions.
Manage special projects and initiatives that advance regional workforce priorities.
Perform other duties as assigned by the Board.

Required Experience:

Experience in workforce development, nonprofit leadership, economic development, education, human resources, public administration, or a related field.
Knowledge of WIOA programs and workforce development systems.
Strong organizational, project management, and facilitation skills.
Demonstrated ability to build relationships and collaborate with diverse stakeholders.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities with limited supervision.
Experience supporting boards, committees, or volunteer leadership groups is highly desirable.

This role offers:

Flexible scheduling and hybrid work arrangements
Meaningful, mission-driven work
Significant autonomy and leadership opportunity
Engagement with regional leaders and workforce partners
The ability to influence workforce strategies that support employers, job seekers, and communities throughout East Central Iowa

Additional Details:

Schedule:
Approximately 25 hours per week, flexible schedule
Location:
Hybrid within the East Central Iowa Workforce Area; occasional work at the American Job Centers in Cedar Rapids and Iowa City
Residency Requirement:
Must reside within the ECIWDB service area, including Benton, Cedar, Iowa, Johnson, Jones, Linn, or Washington County

Interested applicants should submit a cover letter and resume
outlining their qualifications and interest in the position to admin_assist@eciwdb.org
. Applications will be reviewed as they are received and will remain open until the position is filled.
